translations.answer: This is not equivalent to the physics engine not solving ground contact. The project contributor explicitly stated that the restriction is on the static collider contact retrieval/filter API; static collisions still participate in the physics solution. The original version's workaround was to build a large, thin ground surface using RigidObjectCfg + thin CuboidCfg and set kinematic_enabled=True. The original author provided a working configuration, but the thread did not verify that the static filtering restriction has disappeared in subsequent versions, so the upgrade still requires testing.
translations.applicability: Directly applicable to Isaac Sim 4.5.0, Isaac Lab 2.0.0 GPU filtered contact and standard static ground collider; other versions need verification against current PhysX support.
translations.credibility.rationale: Environmental, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: The project contributor suggests adding RigidBodyAPI to the ground prim and enabling the kinematic property.
translations.details.attempts.1: The original author used SceneCfg's RigidObjectCfg/CuboidCfg to create a large, thin ground surface, setting RigidBodyPropertiesCfg(kinematic_enabled=True), collision_props, and friction material.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Distinguish between physics contact solution and contact retrieval/filter API: the maintainer explicitly stated that the static collider's physics collision is still normal, and the restricted is the filtered contact retrieval.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Check if the target prim only has a static collider and no RigidBodyAPI; if using a workaround, confirm that the kinematic body covers all environment areas.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: In the original version, when a filtered contact is needed, replace the standard GroundPlane/static collider with a kinematic rigid body covering the working area; the original author explicitly reported that the RigidObjectCfg configuration is usable.
translations.details.environments.0: Isaac Sim 4.5.0; Isaac Lab 2.0.0; GPU pipeline; /World/ground is a standard static collider.
translations.details.limits.0: This workaround changes the prim type; TerrainImporterCfg, RayCaster's mesh_prim_paths, and multi-environment paths need to be verified separately, and cannot be directly copied.
translations.details.limits.1: Subsequent participants reported prim path and ray-caster mesh errors, but that is not the confirmed fix for the original filtered-contact restriction; this card does not use those comments as a general conclusion.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The original author published the working configuration; Issue was closed after the comment, but the thread did not provide an engine version fix or confirm that the standard static collider filtering is supported.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: ContactSensorCfg reports GPU contact filter not supported and an empty matrix after setting filter_prim_paths_expr on /World/ground; does this mean the ground contact is not being solved by the physics engine?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Do not rely solely on the filtered matrix being zero to determine that the robot is off the ground; use the unfiltered net contact, pose/height, and termination logic for cross-checking.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: At the time, the PhysX GPU contact retrieval API did not support filtering static colliders that are not rigid bodies.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Console warning: GPU contact filter for collider '/World/ground' is not supported.
translations.details.symptoms.1: Cannot retrieve filtered contact data for the static ground after setting filter_prim_paths_expr; normal contact is still usable without the filter.
translations.source.locator: Isaac Lab #1995 comment 2708680265/2711098361's maintainer's restriction note, comment 2877887219's original author's RigidObjectCfg configuration
